t: Look up above the Great West Door of Westminster Abbey. In the niches there stand ten statues, known as the Modern Martyrs, or the twentieth-century martyrs. Among those depicted are Martin Luther King Jr., who pursued civil rights through nonviolence. Dietrich Bonhoeffer is here too, a German pastor who resisted the Nazis and was imprisoned. Maximilian Kolbe, a Polish friar, volunteered to die in another man's place at Auschwitz. Also shown are the Salvadoran archbishop Óscar Romero, Grand Duchess Elizabeth Feodorovna of Russia, and Janani Luwum, a Ugandan archbishop who died shortly after his arrest in 1977.
